relations.myth: Oleg’s men swear by Perun and Volos
relations.note: Volos and Perun jointly witness the Rusʹ oath reported under 907.

relations.myth: Sviatoslav’s oath invokes Perun and Volos
relations.note: They jointly guarantee peace and threaten oath-breakers with divine punishment.
Veles and Perun appear together in a Christian catalogue of false gods.
relations.source: Walk of the Mother of God

relations.note: Reconstructed Veles flees Perun, whose victory releases rain and restores order.
Reconstructed Veles steals Perun’s cattle, wealth, people, family member, or wife.

relations.myth: Mokosh as Veles’s wife or lover
relations.note: Modern reconstructions sometimes identify Mokosh as Veles’s wife or lover.
A further reconstruction names Mokosh as the woman Veles abducts.
Troyan and Veles are jointly listed as beings whom people made gods.
relations.source: Walk of the Mother of God

relations.note: Khors and Veles are jointly listed as beings whom people made gods.
relations.source: Walk of the Mother of God

relations.note: Stryjkowski compares Vlos with the classical pastoral god Pan.
Stryjkowski compares Vlos with the classical woodland god Faunus.
Baltic-Slavic reconstruction compares Veles with Lithuanian Velnias.
Comparativists equate Veles with Vala as an adversary of the thunderer.
Comparativists equate Veles with Vṛtra as an adversary of the thunderer.
A contested comparison links Veles with Varuṇa through oaths and cosmic order.
Modern neopagan and occult communities treat Veles as corresponding to Odin.
Modern occult reception assimilates Veles to the horned god Cernunnos.
Modern cross-traditional systems propose a correspondence between Veles and Hermes.
Modern occult systems compare underworld-associated Veles with Hades.
